chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd Abī al-Khazraj, from Faḍl ibn ʿUthmān al-Aʿwar, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام, concerning:

A man is killed, and his head is found in one tribe, and his middle and chest in another tribe, and the rest in another tribe. He said: “His diyah is upon the one in whose tribe his chest and body are found, and the salat (prayer) is to be performed over him.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the funeral prayer to be performed over the deceased
key_terms.دِيَتُهُ: his blood-money compensation due for unlawful killing
key_terms.صَدْرُهُ: his chest, the determining bodily section for legal attribution here
key_terms.قَبِيلَةٍ: a tribe or tribal jurisdiction in which the body part is found

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for the diyah if a murdered person’s body parts are found in different tribes?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability for the diyah when the dismembered body of a slain man is found distributed among different tribes. It assigns responsibility based on the location of the chest and body, and it also affirms that salat (prayer) is performed over the deceased.
